about.title: San Fernando Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: San Fernando is a small city, but its traffic corridors carry a steady flow of commuters and local drivers every day. Public records show 81 injury collisions and 116 injured people in the most recent final crash year, with reported crashes clustering on Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. — a pattern that lines up with rush-hour traffic on Truman Street, San Fernando Road, Glenoaks Boulevard, and N Maclay Avenue. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the days right after matter: photos fade from memory, vehicles get repaired or scrapped, and insurance adjusters start building their file before you've even seen a doctor. We handle car accident claims on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Our job is to help you sort out what happened and what comes next.

whyChoose.title: Why San Fernando Drivers Choose Us

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim, but if a government vehicle or agency is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Waiting too long to talk to someone can close doors you didn't know were there.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for a crash on Glenoaks Boulevard or elsewhere, you may still recover a reduced share of damages. We can help make sure your side of the story is properly documented.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life in most car accident cases. That's one more reason not to settle quickly on a number the insurance company suggests.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. We can advise you on what, if anything, you need to say.

items.question: What if my crash happened at a busy time on San Fernando Road or Truman Street?
items.answer: Crash reports and any available traffic camera or dashcam footage from that stretch of road can be valuable evidence, especially during peak Thursday evening hours when reported collisions tend to cluster. The sooner this evidence is preserved, the easier it is for us to piece together what happened.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing — we offer free consultations, and we work on contingency. That means there's no fee unless you recover compensation for your injuries.
